title: Call Tracking for Affiliates: How It Works
h1: Call tracking for affiliates: how it works and what to look for
description: Call tracking for affiliates explained: tracking numbers, routing, quality and payouts. See what to look for before sending live calls.
faq: What is call tracking for affiliates?
It gives each traffic source its own phone number so every call is credited to the right affiliate, campaign and payout rate, with a record you can check.
How do affiliates get paid for phone calls?
The network sets a payout rate per affiliate and defines which calls are payable, such as a minimum duration and location. Payouts are then calculated from the call record and shown on a statement.
Do I need my own tracking numbers as an affiliate?
Using a separate number per source or campaign is the cleanest way to prove where calls came from and to compare sources by calls rather than clicks.
body:
Call tracking for affiliates means giving every traffic source its own phone number, so each call is credited to the right affiliate, the right campaign and the right payout rate the moment it comes in. If you promote pay-per-call offers, it is the difference between being paid for calls you can prove and arguing about calls you can only remember.

Why affiliates need call tracking

A click leaves a trail. A phone call, by default, does not. When a visitor reads your page and then dials a number, nothing links that call back to you unless the number itself carries the attribution. Without tracking you end up relying on the buyer's own count, and the buyer's count may not match yours.

Good call tracking gives you three things: proof of which source sent each call, a record of how long it lasted and what happened on it, and a way to see your earnings without asking anyone.

How call tracking for affiliates works

Tracking numbers and dynamic number insertion

With dynamic number insertion, the phone number shown on your page changes depending on the visitor's source. One visitor sees one number, another visitor sees a different one, and each call can be traced back to the source behind it. That lets you compare traffic sources by calls, not just by clicks.

Routing to the buyer

Once a call arrives, rules decide where it goes: which buyer is open, what their daily cap is, which states they take, and which numbers are blocked. A pre-transfer check can confirm the buyer is available before the caller is connected, which protects the caller experience and your reputation as a source.

Quality and payouts

Quality is what keeps a source in the program. Short calls, repeat callers and blocked numbers are the usual reasons a buyer pushes back. Seeing quality per source lets you fix a weak placement before it costs you a relationship. Payouts then follow from the same record: a rate per affiliate, applied to the calls that meet the written rules.

What to look for as an affiliate

  • Your own numbers. Each source or campaign should have its own tracking number.
  • A portal you can log into. You should see your own calls and earnings without sending a message.
  • Clear payable-call rules. Minimum duration, location, repeats and blocked numbers should be written down before traffic starts.
  • Statements you can download. A statement built from the same data you can see removes most disputes.
  • Quality feedback. Knowing a source is drifting toward short calls lets you act early.

If you also want to understand the money side from the network's point of view, read how pay per call affiliate payouts work.

How this works in Insight Dial

Insight Dial is a pay-per-call platform, and the pieces above map to features you can look at on the call tracking and payouts sections of the features page:

  1. The network you work with sets up a campaign with country and state targeting, then adds you as an affiliate with your own payout rate.
  2. You get tracking numbers, with dynamic number insertion so calls are tied to the source on your page.
  3. Calls are routed by rules such as hours, daily caps, blocked numbers and repeat-caller blocks.
  4. Quality grades of Good, Watch or Poor show how a source is performing, and sources sending too many short calls can be paused automatically.
  5. In the affiliate portal you can see your calls and earnings and download statements.

The product page shows the whole flow, and pricing explains the pay-as-you-go model. If your offers are in a particular vertical, the industry pages for insurance and home services show how those campaigns are usually structured.

Common mistakes to avoid

The first is sharing one number across every source. You lose attribution, and every dispute becomes one person's word against another's. The second is leaving the payable-call rules vague: if nobody has written down the minimum duration or how repeat callers are treated, each side will assume the version that suits them. The third is only looking at volume. A source that sends many short calls can look good in a weekly total and still damage the relationship with a buyer, so watch quality alongside count. Finally, do not wait for a payout date to check your numbers; reviewing calls as they arrive keeps small differences from piling up.

Before you send live traffic

Place a test call and confirm it appears against the right source with the right rate. Check that the number shown on your page is the one you were given. Confirm the payable-call rules in writing. A few minutes of testing is cheaper than a week of calls that cannot be credited.

Call recording and do-not-call rules differ by place and by vertical, so check your obligations with your own counsel before you run traffic.

Next step

If you promote pay-per-call offers, you can apply as an affiliate. If you run the campaigns and want to onboard affiliates, you can create a publisher account or book a 30-minute demo.
